Rarely seen above ground, the gorr digs deep connected tunnels with its own kind, building vast communal burrows. Th ese near-blind 
lizards navigate the dark using two methods: Primarily sniffi ng for fresh tubers and the musty smell of tasty booralugs, that are often 
found attached to the top of wet cave ceilings, eating the bacteria that permeates throughout the Umbrawells. Th e second, a much 
more unique method that has been adapted by the static that they build up in their scales from shuffling along iron-rich stone caverns. 
Sensitive sensors run along their muzzle tingle with the proximity of nearby predators. Periodically the static builds up can release a 
lethal discharge when the animal feels an excessive amount of stress.
